open_points.subject: Owner-session cookie on local access
open_points.text: The cookie is “sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine”; the text does not say whether it is Secure-only when Registry is reached locally without HTTPS.
open_points.question: May an owner-session cookie be sent over local HTTP, or must every owner-interface origin use HTTPS?
options: Allow the cookie over HTTP only for local access
Require HTTPS and a Secure cookie for every access
Choose the cookie attributes according to how the current request reached Registry
open_points.default_guess: Require HTTPS and a Secure cookie for every access.

open_points.subject: Concurrent sign-out and admitted owner requests
open_points.text: A request that passes the session check “completes even if … a sign-out comes while it runs”, but session-changing requests are ordered by the session lock and “each sees the session as the one before left it”; the text also says one admitted before sign-out completes its change.
open_points.question: If a request passes the session check, then sign-out takes the session lock first, may the earlier admitted request still mutate the store after sign-out?
options: Every request admitted before sign-out may finish regardless of lock order
Lock order controls, so sign-out first invalidates the waiting request
Sign-out waits for all previously admitted requests before ending the session
open_points.default_guess: Every request admitted before sign-out may finish, and sign-out is ordered after already admitted changes.

open_points.subject: Confirmation-input digest
open_points.text: Import inputs are kept “as a digest of those values in a fixed order”, but neither the order, canonical encoding nor digest algorithm is declared.
open_points.question: How are the action, target, revision or access version, picks and input values canonically encoded and digested for confirmation binding?
options: Canonical JSON with a declared field order and hash
Length-prefixed binary fields in a declared order
Digest the eventual HTTP form encoding
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical JSON with explicitly ordered fields and SHA-256.

open_points.subject: Atomicity of confirmation consumption
open_points.text: A04 says “Every action is atomic: it applies all its changes or none”, while A13 says a matching confirmation value “is used up by the first submission that carries it, whatever its answer”, including a refused action.
open_points.question: Is consuming the pending confirmation outside the atomic domain action, so a refused action may still change the owner session?
options: Domain changes are atomic, but confirmation consumption is an independent session change
Confirmation consumption and the domain action are one transaction and both roll back on refusal
The combined transaction commits confirmation consumption even when it commits no domain change
open_points.default_guess: Treat confirmation consumption as an independent session change and atomicity as applying to the domain action.

open_points.subject: Failures within one validation stage
open_points.text: A04 says checks occur in order and the first failure is the answer, but also says “When several checks of one stage fail, the answer names every one of them.” Stage 1 contains authentication, CSRF and confirmation checks, although CSRF and confirmation cannot be safely evaluated without a valid session.
open_points.question: Must checks within a stage short-circuit in their listed order, or must Registry aggregate all failures in that stage?
options: Short-circuit within each stage
Aggregate every evaluable failure in the stage
Aggregate all failures, treating unavailable session-bound checks as failures too
open_points.default_guess: Short-circuit authentication before evaluating session-bound CSRF or confirmation values.

open_points.subject: Import versus concurrent ordinary writes
open_points.text: A16 serialises concurrent import confirmations and makes one import transaction, but does not order that transaction against concurrent project, room, pointer or customer writes that can create a conflict after the confirmation checks.
open_points.question: What result is required when an ordinary write races the import between its conflict check and commit?
options: Serialize the import with every potentially conflicting write
Allow one transaction to fail at commit and return a conflict
Take a store-wide import lock from confirmation checking through commit
open_points.default_guess: Serialize the import transaction with every write that can affect its checked records or identifiers.

open_points.subject: Migration file digest
open_points.text: The mapping and migration closure name the file “by its digest”, but the digest algorithm and whether it covers the exact uploaded bytes or a parsed canonical representation are not stated.
open_points.question: How is the migration file digest calculated?
options: Hash the exact uploaded bytes
Hash a canonical serialization of the parsed file
Store both a byte digest and a canonical-content digest
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: Configuration variable schema
open_points.text: The configuration is “the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_” and each item must be “well formed”, but the exact variable names and the well-formedness rules for locations and secrets are not declared.
open_points.question: What are the exact environment-variable names and validation grammar for every A17 configuration item?
options: Declare one fixed variable name and grammar per item
Accept several aliases for each item
Derive names from service names and treat all values as unrestricted strings except paths
open_points.default_guess: Declare one fixed REGISTRY_-prefixed name and explicit grammar per item.

open_points.subject: Secret length measurement
open_points.text: Each secret must be “at least 32 bytes long”, but environment variables are text and the text does not define their encoding or whether secrets are restricted to a byte-safe alphabet.
open_points.question: How is the 32-byte minimum measured for an environment-variable secret?
options: UTF-8 encoded byte length
Decoded byte length of a required Base64 value
Character count restricted to ASCII
open_points.default_guess: Require Base64-encoded random bytes and measure the decoded value.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption format
open_points.text: A backup is required to be encrypted with the backup key and unreadable without it, but no authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce rule, key derivation, format version or authentication requirement is declared.
open_points.question: What cryptographic format makes a backup encrypted and detects ciphertext or metadata alteration?
options: A declared AEAD format using the configured key directly
A declared KDF plus AEAD format with per-backup salt and nonce
Implementation-selected encryption with a separate plaintext digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned format with a standard KDF and AEAD, with a fresh salt and nonce per backup and authenticated metadata.

open_points.subject: Backup-key rotation and old backups
open_points.text: “Older backups stay encrypted with the key they were made with”, but configuration holds only one backup key and the digest merely names the old key; the text does not say where an old key is retained or how an old backup can be restored or rechecked.
open_points.question: After key rotation, how can a kept backup made with an earlier key be decrypted?
options: The owner must retain every old key outside Registry
Configuration may contain a key ring of current and retained keys
Old backups are re-encrypted with the new key
Old backups remain kept but are intentionally unrestorable
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to retain old keys outside Registry for at least as long as their backups are kept.

open_points.subject: Unreadable kept backups after key rotation
open_points.text: A run deletes “every file under the kept prefix that cannot be read as a backup”, while an older backup may not be decryptable with the current configured key but is supposed to stay encrypted with its old key.
open_points.question: Does “read as a backup” mean parsing its unencrypted envelope, or successfully authenticating and decrypting it with an available key?
options: Only the unencrypted envelope must parse
The complete backup must decrypt and validate
Old-key backups are exempt when their envelope names another key digest
open_points.default_guess: Treat a file as a backup when its versioned envelope parses; do not delete it merely because the current key cannot decrypt it.

open_points.subject: Backup audit sequence for a new store
open_points.text: Every backup records “the last audit sequence number it holds” and checks that the log ends there, but a new store may have no audit entry and no last sequence number.
open_points.question: What value is recorded and checked when the audit log is empty?
options: Record 0
Record an explicit null or absent value
Do not permit a backup until an audit entry exists
open_points.default_guess: Record 0 and require the restored log to contain no entries.

open_points.subject: Claim that Registry makes daily backups
open_points.text: R0-89 says “Registry makes daily encrypted backups and checks each one”, while A18 says a missed 03:00, an overlapping run, an owner-only start or a stopped Registry makes no run, and failed runs may produce no kept backup.
open_points.question: Is a checked backup guaranteed for every calendar day, or is only one best-effort run scheduled daily with the stated skip and failure cases?
options: Guarantee one checked backup per calendar day with catch-up
Schedule one best-effort attempt at 03:00 with no catch-up
Describe days without a successful run as violating Registry's guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Treat A18 as controlling: schedule one best-effort attempt at 03:00 with no catch-up.

open_points.subject: Uploaded files in other owner sessions after import
open_points.text: Changed M11 says an uploaded import file is “dropped when the import is accepted”, while A16 says “a file another session keeps stays until that session ends” after another session accepts the import.
open_points.question: Does accepting the import discard uploaded import files from every owner session or only from the session that confirmed it?
options: Discard every session's uploaded import file
Discard only the confirming session's file
Keep every file, including the confirming session's, until its session ends
open_points.default_guess: Discard only the confirming session's file; leave other sessions' files until those sessions end.
